items.text: Mentions can leave out a namesake: add words under "Skip if it also says" for the brand or a competitor, and posts, videos and episodes that also say one aren't kept. New mentions that say one are cleared on the next scan.

YouTube and podcast mentions now search competitors with a real name first, and each scan carries on where the last stopped, so every competitor gets searched over a few scans instead of only the first ones in alphabetical order.

Connect Linear, Notion or ClickUp, read only, and agents can search and read your issues, tasks, projects and docs when they need them, so they know what the team is working on and what it decided. Nothing is copied into Outflare, and nothing in your tools changes.

Tags behave the same everywhere. On saved search reports and brand assets, as on other saved reports, a tag that repeats another in different capitals is dropped, extra spaces are tidied, and an empty tag is ignored rather than refused.

Lifetime value and Distribution reports now have a Filter button, so you can count only some payments, such as one product or one first channel. On Lifetime value, click any number of customers to see who they are, with what each has paid.

Support is now an area of its own in the menu, with Conversations, Saved replies, Reports, Help centre and Settings as pages. The Inbox holds only replies to your outreach. Old links to a support conversation or the help centre open in their new place.

Two-factor sign-in: add an authenticator app under Your account and type its code after your password, with ten backup codes for a lost phone, and "Remember this device for 7 days" so a trusted browser isn't asked every time. An owner can require it for everyone in the workspace, and reset it for a member who is locked out. Signing in with a passkey already counts.
A chat can show an AI reply that is sent through a tool while it is being written: Outflare's AI layer now streams tool calls as well as text, for Claude and OpenAI-compatible models.

The agent's chat shows a reply while it is being written, and long conversations keep working instead of being cut off. You can rate a reply, ask for it again, edit your last message, see the sources behind a reply, get charts in replies, and print a chat or save it as a PDF or Word file.

Lifetime value can count from the first time a customer did an event, such as signing up, instead of from their first payment. Customers who never paid count too, so the average is what a sign-up is worth. Pick it under "Customers who first" on the Lifetime value page; agents pass `start_event` to `run_lifetime_value`.

Balances can be split by a field of the customer or their company, such as plan or country. Pick it under "Split by" to see what each group holds, how many customers it has and how much sits untouched, and click a group to list its customers. Agents pass `breakdown` to `run_balance`.

Staff now suggests people, details and leavers from your Google Workspace, and payments from a bank statement you pick as CSV (read in your browser, never uploaded); nothing changes until an owner accepts. Owners can also edit Staff's lists, such as person types.

Dashboard templates: the Dashboards page now offers ready-made dashboards you add in one click. The first is a management report built from your payments: revenue, new customers, revenue by product, order value, lifetime value and money kept. Every report in it is yours to change. Agents use `list_dashboard_templates`.

Every saved report has its own address. Lifecycle and stickiness questions and saved Tracker reports now open straight from All reports, a link or a reload, where before they opened the page and left you to find the report. Revenue and a campaign's spend also show the amount in the period before next to the change.

Team directory: owners can now keep contact details, contracts, pay and payments for everyone who works for the company, people and organisations alike (employees, freelancers, contractors, agencies, service providers), with a change log, a monthly pay summary and a CSV export. Only owners can see it, enforced on the server.

Finances: a new section that shows the whole company's money in and out across every brand, in US dollars, with profit, margin, the last 12 months, each brand and where the money goes. It adds up what Outflare already records, so nothing needs connecting. Only owners see it unless an owner gives the Finances permission.
A connection to an outside MCP server can be kept to owners: only owners see and use its tools, and an agent can use them only while it answers an owner.

Distribution can show how usage is spread, not only payments: pick "Times they did an event" or "Usage: a number on an event" to see how many customers use a little and how many a lot, and how much of all usage the top tenth carry. Agents pass `event_count` or `event_total` with `event` to `run_distribution`.
Anyone who can add tasks can now note a decision on a goal, including agents. Changing or replacing a decision still needs the permission to manage goals.

Our team: everyone in the company now sees who works here, with their photo, position, department, what they look after, work email, Telegram, GitHub and Slack. Members are linked to the staff directory by work email, so nobody is entered twice, and adding someone to Staff can also invite them to Outflare.
Balances shows how long the amount held would last: "Lasts about" is what is held now divided by the last 30 days' rate of use. Agents read it as `days_of_use` from `run_balance`.

Roles per brand: someone can now be on a different role for single brands, such as a viewer of the workspace who is a Member on one brand, or a Member who only views another. Open a person under Settings, Members to pick a role for each brand. On that brand its role decides what they can do, and API tokens they made follow it.
The Agents page has a side column in place of its row of tabs: what waits for you, the history and what agents may do each open from it, and each has its own address.

The menu now follows the parts of a business: Customers, Growth, Support and Analytics for the brand you picked, then the company's own sections. Email, search, social, ads, partnerships and automations sit together under Growth. Replies to outreach moved from the top of the menu to Growth, Outreach, Replies; old Inbox links still open them.

Sales emails from your own mailbox, including sequences, are no longer refused because the person is on a customer list, a partner list or a sequencer's outreach blocklist. Those only keep people out of cold email. A refusal now names the address and the reason, such as unsubscribed or bounced, and clears when you pick another address.
Security improvements to sign-in.
Podcast mentions read transcripts written by speech to text tools as JSON, and quote what was said instead of the transcript's code.

Distribution: Total paid now starts as what customers paid, with refunds left out, so no range starts below zero. A new Refunds control switches between gross and net, and with refunds taken off the first range reads "Under $10". The Management report template's tile counts the same way.

Support has its own permission, separate from the Inbox: a role can now see and answer support conversations without seeing replies to outreach, or the other way round. Everyone who could use the Inbox keeps Support until you change their role under Settings, Roles. API tokens use the new `support.read` and `support.manage` scopes.

Finances can show the company's money in your own currency: an owner picks it on the Money page (US dollars until then), and every brand's money is converted at each day's exchange rate. Cost categories now have the same names on the Money and Outcomes pages.

Sales templates can be for every source or only for conversations from chosen Sales channels, and writing a message starts by picking one (or writing from scratch). Templates and sequences fill in more fields, including the person's own form answers, with fallbacks, and the sequence preview shows which fields were empty.

Sales lists and conversations show each lead's email address under the name, with a copy button, and the lists can be searched by email, name or company. From a person's page, a Sales rep can email them or add them to a sequence: it opens the rep's own Sales conversation with them, or says which teammate holds it.
